Collectors._ApplyFilter_comment: When false: collect ALL logs (no filtering). When true: only collect events matching the filters below.
Collectors._WindowsEventLogFilter_comment: Event IDs collected per channel when ApplyFilter=true. Covers Kiwi Syslog + Motodata standard sets (MITRE/NIST/CIS).

Collectors._LinuxJournaldMaxPriority_comment: Priority filter when ApplyFilter=true. 0=Emergency, 1=Alert, 2=Critical, 3=Error, 4=Warning, 5=Notice, 6=Info, 7=Debug. Default 4 captures Emergency through Warning.
Collectors._LinuxJournaldUnits_comment: Systemd units to monitor when ApplyFilter=true. Covers Kiwi/Motodata standard set.

_LinuxJournaldUnits_descriptions.sshd: SSH Daemon — remote login attempts, accepted/rejected connections
_LinuxJournaldUnits_descriptions.sudo: Sudo — privilege escalation events, who ran what as root
_LinuxJournaldUnits_descriptions.systemd: Core Systemd — service start/stop/fail, dependency events, boot sequence
_LinuxJournaldUnits_descriptions.systemd-logind: Login Manager — user session start/stop, seat management
_LinuxJournaldUnits_descriptions.systemd-journald: Journal Daemon — journal rotation, corruption, disk space warnings
_LinuxJournaldUnits_descriptions.NetworkManager: Network Manager — interface up/down, IP changes, WiFi/VPN events
_LinuxJournaldUnits_descriptions.firewalld: Firewall Daemon (RHEL/CentOS) — rule changes, blocked connections
_LinuxJournaldUnits_descriptions.ufw: Uncomplicated Firewall (Ubuntu/Debian) — rule changes, blocked connections
_LinuxJournaldUnits_descriptions.auditd: Audit Daemon — kernel-level security auditing (file access, syscalls)
_LinuxJournaldUnits_descriptions.polkitd: PolicyKit — authorization decisions for system actions
_LinuxJournaldUnits_descriptions.cron: Cron Scheduler (Debian/Ubuntu) — scheduled job execution and failures
_LinuxJournaldUnits_descriptions.crond: Cron Scheduler (RHEL/CentOS) — scheduled job execution and failures
_LinuxJournaldUnits_descriptions.atd: At Daemon — one-time scheduled job execution
_LinuxJournaldUnits_descriptions.containerd: Container Runtime — low-level container lifecycle events
_LinuxJournaldUnits_descriptions.kubelet: Kubernetes Node Agent — pod scheduling, health checks, failures
_LinuxJournaldUnits_descriptions.fail2ban: Fail2Ban — intrusion prevention, IP bans, brute-force detection
_LinuxJournaldUnits_descriptions.apparmor: AppArmor — mandatory access control denials and profile events
_LinuxJournaldUnits_descriptions.dovecot: Dovecot IMAP/POP3 — mailbox access, authentication events
_LinuxJournaldUnits_descriptions.chronyd: Chrony NTP Client — time synchronization events
_LinuxJournaldUnits_descriptions.smartd: SMART Daemon — disk health monitoring, failure prediction
_LinuxJournaldUnits_descriptions.mdmonitor: MD RAID Monitor — software RAID array health events

Collectors._LinuxJournaldUnits_extended_comment: Additional units added beyond the base set — databases, VPN, directory services, device mgmt.
Collectors._LinuxSyslogFiles_comment: Explicit log files to monitor with per-file offset tracking. Covers all major distros. LinuxAutoDiscoverLogs=true adds any additional files found under /var/log/ automatically.

_LinuxSyslogFiles_descriptions./var/log/syslog: Main system log (Debian/Ubuntu) — all facility messages
_LinuxSyslogFiles_descriptions./var/log/messages: Main system log (RHEL/CentOS) — all facility messages
_LinuxSyslogFiles_descriptions./var/log/auth.log: Authentication log (Debian/Ubuntu) — SSH, sudo, PAM events
_LinuxSyslogFiles_descriptions./var/log/secure: Authentication log (RHEL/CentOS) — SSH, sudo, PAM events
_LinuxSyslogFiles_descriptions./var/log/kern.log: Kernel messages — hardware errors, driver issues, segfaults, OOM kills
_LinuxSyslogFiles_descriptions./var/log/audit/audit.log: Auditd log — kernel-level file access, syscall, user command auditing
_LinuxSyslogFiles_descriptions./var/log/boot.log: Boot messages — service startup during boot sequence
_LinuxSyslogFiles_descriptions./var/log/firewalld: Firewalld log (RHEL/CentOS) — rule changes and blocked connections
_LinuxSyslogFiles_descriptions./var/log/fail2ban.log: Fail2Ban log — IP bans, unban, brute-force detection events
_LinuxSyslogFiles_descriptions./var/log/nginx/access.log: Nginx access log — HTTP requests, status codes, client IPs
_LinuxSyslogFiles_descriptions./var/log/nginx/error.log: Nginx error log — server errors, upstream failures

Collectors._LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_comment: Regex patterns applied when ApplyFilter=true. Covers Kiwi/Motodata standard detection patterns.

_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.sshd: SSH daemon activity — login attempts, key auth, disconnects
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.sudo: Privilege escalation — commands run with sudo
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.authentication failure: PAM authentication failures — wrong password, locked account
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.session opened: User session started — login via SSH, console, or su
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.pam_unix: PAM module events — authentication, account, session management
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.pam_systemd: PAM systemd events — session registration with systemd
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.segfault: Segmentation fault — process crashed due to memory violation
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.oom-killer: Out-of-Memory killer — kernel terminated a process to free memory
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.kernel.*panic: Kernel panic — system crash, unrecoverable error
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.kernel.*warning: Kernel warnings — non-fatal but notable issues
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.kernel.*oops: Kernel oops — non-fatal kernel error, potential instability
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.iptables: iptables firewall rule matches — blocked/allowed packets
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.nftables: nftables firewall rule matches (modern replacement for iptables)
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.UFW: Ubuntu Uncomplicated Firewall log entries — blocked connections
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.fail2ban: Fail2Ban actions — IP bans/unbans from brute-force detection
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.apparmor: AppArmor MAC — profile enforcement, denied access attempts
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.avc:.*denied: SELinux Access Vector Cache — mandatory access control denial
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.selinux: SELinux events — policy enforcement, mode changes
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.COMMAND=: Sudo command logging — exact command executed with sudo
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.forbidden: Forbidden access — HTTP 403 or policy rejection
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.connection refused: Network connection refused — service down or firewall block
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.error: Generic error events across all services
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.readonly: Filesystem mounted read-only — possible disk failure
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.I/O error: Disk I/O error — hardware failure indicator
_LinuxSyslogFilePatterns_descriptions.killed process: Process killed by kernel (OOM or signal)

Collectors._LinuxDmesg_comment: Enable dmesg batch collector for kernel ring buffer. Only needed on non-journald systems (Alpine, minimal containers). When journald is present it already covers kernel messages.
Collectors._LinuxBinaryLogs_comment: Enable collection of binary login records (wtmp/btmp/lastlog) via last/lastb/lastlog commands. btmp collection requires root privileges.
Collectors._LinuxAutoDiscoverLogs_comment: Automatically discover and collect ALL text log files under /var/log/ and subdirectories. Covers database logs, custom app logs, and any file not in LinuxSyslogFiles. New files are picked up without restart.
